name: Monticello Historic District
unique: A courthouse town of brick storefronts and antebellum and Victorian houses on a grid of live oak streets, in the county seat of one of the oldest cotton counties in Florida, twenty five miles east of Tallahassee.
buzz: The houses are the attraction and the town is quiet enough to walk alone. People who live in Tallahassee drive over for the square and the bed and breakfast.

name: Letchworth-Love Mounds Archaeological State Park
unique: The tallest Native American ceremonial mound in Florida, a fifty one foot platform mound built by people of the Weeden Island culture more than a thousand years ago, with a museum and a trail through the earthworks.
buzz: The mound is bigger than people expect for Florida and the interpretation is careful about what is known and what is not. It is quiet, cheap and usually empty.

name: Wacissa River
dates: Year round, best spring and fall
company: Local outfitters and the Northwest Florida Water Management District
unique: A spring fed river running clear and fast out of a swamp north of the Aucilla, with a public ramp, eelgrass and turtles visible from the boat and enough current to make the paddle downstream effortless.
buzz: Paddlers call it the clearest small river in north Florida and the alligators are numerous and calm. Outfitters run shuttles from Wacissa and the summer weekends get busy.

name: Madison Historic District
unique: A courthouse square with a ring of 1800s commercial buildings and streets of Greek Revival, Italianate and Victorian houses, in a cotton town that was one of the richest in antebellum Florida.
buzz: Architectural historians rank the district among the best small town collections in the state. The square and the four streets around it take an afternoon and there is almost nobody else walking.

name: Madison Blue Spring State Park
unique: A first magnitude spring that pours into the Withlacoochee River in a limestone bowl, with a swimming area, a dive platform and a cave system that makes it a certification site for cave divers.
buzz: Swimmers like the bowl shape and the river that runs out of it, and divers come for the cavern. The park is small and the parking fills early on summer weekends.

name: St. Andrews State Park
unique: A park on the pass between the Gulf and St. Andrews Bay with a jettied channel where the water is clear and calm, two beaches, a campground behind the dunes and a ferry to Shell Island.
buzz: The gulf side surf fishes and the bay side is where families snorkel with children because the jetties hold the waves back. Shell Island is the boat trip everybody takes.

name: Man in the Sea Museum
unique: A small museum of diving history on the site of the Navy's first experimental diving unit, with a submarine, a diving bell, helmets and suits and the story of how saturation diving and the SEALAB programs were worked out here.
buzz: Divers and Navy people come for the equipment and children like the submarine they can climb into. It is small, cheap and run by volunteers who know the history firsthand.

name: Silver Springs State Park
dates: Year round, boats on a schedule
customer: Families, glass bottom boat riders, paddlers
unique: Florida's oldest attraction, a first magnitude spring pouring into the Silver River, with glass bottom boats over the spring vents, rhesus macaques and manatees in the run, and kayak rentals to paddle it yourself.
buzz: The glass bottom boat is the classic and the monkeys on the riverbank are the thing children remember. Paddlers go early to beat the boats and see the most wildlife.

name: Juniper Springs Recreation Area
company: U.S. Forest Service, Ocala National Forest
unique: A spring built into a CCC era stone and concrete swimming basin with a mill house and a run that paddlers follow downstream through the Ocala National Forest to Juniper Creek.
buzz: The stone basin is beautiful and the water is cold, and the paddle down Juniper Creek is a half day of narrow twisting water. It is the busiest spring in the forest and still worth it on a weekday.

name: Mount Dora
unique: A hilltop town on Lake Dora with brick streets, Victorian storefronts, antique shops, a lighthouse and a lakefront park where seaplanes come and go, forty minutes from Orlando and a different century.
buzz: The antique shops and the restaurants are the draw and the lakefront is the reward. It is busy on winter weekends with people escaping the north and quiet in July.

name: Lake Louisa State Park
unique: Four thousand acres of rolling sandhill, lake and cypress swamp west of Orlando, with a chain of lakes, cabins and a campground, horse trails and paved cycling, in country that looks like the hills of north Florida.
buzz: It is the camping park for Orlando and the hills surprise people who think central Florida is flat. The cabins book out and the lakes are quiet on weekdays.

name: De Soto National Memorial
unique: The presumed landing site of Hernando de Soto's 1539 expedition, with a visitor center on the conquest of La Florida, a living history camp in season where rangers wear armor, and a trail along the Manatee River.
buzz: The rangers in period armor are the part children remember and the exhibits do not romanticize the expedition. It is free, on the water and rarely crowded.

name: Cortez Fishing Village
company: Cortez Village and the Florida Maritime Museum
unique: One of the last working fishing villages on Florida's west coast, with net sheds, docks, a maritime museum in a 1912 schoolhouse and seafood houses that sell what the boats brought in.
buzz: The mullet and stone crab are the point and the village has kept its scale. People come for lunch and stay to walk the docks.

name: National Navy UDT-SEAL Museum
unique: The only museum dedicated to the Navy's underwater demolition teams and SEALs, on the beach where they trained in World War Two, with boats, diving gear, weapons, a helicopter and the memorial wall.
buzz: Veterans come and the volunteers are often former operators, which makes the tour personal. The vehicles and the beach outside are the two things people mention.

name: Fort Pierce Inlet State Park
unique: A barrier island park where the Indian River lagoon meets the Atlantic at the inlet, with a swimming beach on the ocean side, a calm lagoon beach for children and a jetty where the fishing and snorkeling are good.
buzz: The lagoon side is the family beach and the ocean side is where the surf is. It is quieter than the public beaches in town and the inlet is the reason the water is clear.

name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park
unique: Eleven thousand acres of sand pine scrub, river swamp and mangrove along the Loxahatchee River, with a canoe trail through a federally designated wild and scenic river, a campground and a hill that is actually a hill.
buzz: The Loxahatchee paddle is the reason to come and the cypress swamp upstream is the best part of it. Cyclists use the paved roads and the campground is one of the biggest in the state.

name: Stuart Riverwalk and Downtown
unique: A riverfront town on the St. Lucie with a boardwalk along the water, a downtown of brick storefronts and a reputation as the sailfish capital of the world, with the fleet docks a few blocks away.
buzz: The riverwalk is where the town runs and the restaurants face the water. In sailfish season the docks are full of sportfishing boats and the bars are full of crews.

name: Pelican Island National Wildlife Refuge
unique: America's first national wildlife refuge, set aside by Theodore Roosevelt in 1903 to protect the brown pelicans nesting on a small mangrove island, now surrounded by a lagoon of seagrass, manatees and more than a hundred bird species.
buzz: The island itself is closed to landing, which people learn to respect, and the viewing platform and the Centennial Trail give the birds up close. Birders come in winter for the pelicans and the roseate spoonbills.

name: McKee Botanical Garden
unique: Eighteen acres of tropical hammock and water lilies planted in the 1920s as a roadside attraction, with a stone bridge, a hall of ferns, a children's garden and a giant water lily pond.
buzz: The water lilies and the old stone work are the photographs and the children's garden keeps families there longer than planned. It is a 1920s roadside garden that survived and got better.

name: Paynes Creek Historic State Park
unique: The site of a trading post and fort built in 1849 after the last outbreak of the Second Seminole War, where two storekeepers were killed, with a museum, earthworks and a trail along Paynes Creek.
buzz: It is small, free and almost unknown, and the story of a fort built for a war that was already ending is the interesting part. The creek is good for a short walk.

name: Wauchula Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1920s courthouse and a ring of storefronts in a county built on cattle, citrus and the Peace River, in a town whose name comes from a Creek word for wild turkey.
buzz: Two blocks and a diner, and the people are used to nobody stopping. The square is shaded and the courthouse lawn is where the town gathers.
